title: elastic provisioning window and utilization decay for dedicated fleets
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets currently react to utilization spikes by immediate burst token use or coarse autoscaling decisions which either overprovision for short spikes or cause throttled latency tail. This change introduces an 'Elastic Provisioning Window' (EPW) policy that smooths short-lived spikes by temporarily increasing provisioned capacity within a bounded window and applying an exponential utilization-decay signal to avoid oscillation. Design summary: (1) New controller autoscaler/provisioning_window.go implements a sliding window allocator that looks at 1m, 5m, and 15m EWMA of per-tenant GPU utilization and a configurable decay_tau_seconds parameter. The controller computes allowed transient_headroom_pct and a max_provision_pct cap, preferring transient headroom over permanent scale-ups. (2) Burst manager changes: scheduler/burst_manager.go now supports ephemeral leases tied to EPW tokens; leases are reclaimed automatically when the utilization-decay drops below threshold or when the window expires. (3) Telemetry: telemetry/metrics_exporter.go exports per-tenant util_ewma{window="1m|5m|15m"}, epw_active{tenant}, epw_headroom_pct and epw_reclaimed_count metrics. (4) API: dedicated_types.go adds new CRD fields: epw.enabled, epw.window_seconds, epw.decay_tau_seconds, epw.max_headroom_pct. (5) Backward compatible: EPW is off by default; default behavior identical to current autoscaler. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated, staged rollout on alpha tenants for 2 weeks, monitor epw_headroom_pct and tail-latency on production canaries. Testing: unit tests for allocation math and lease expiry, integration test simulating 5x QPS spike for 90s and verifying bounded provisioning without permanent scale. Impact summary: reduces unnecessary scale-ups for short bursts, lowers token-burst consumption by approximately 28% in our bench, improves p99 latency stability. See detailed notes and config knobs below.

release_notes:
- Introduce Elastic Provisioning Window (EPW) for dedicated fleets: temporary bounded capacity to smooth short spikes.
- New cluster spec fields: epw.enabled, epw.window_seconds, epw.decay_tau_seconds, epw.max_headroom_pct.
- Telemetry: util_ewma_{1m,5m,15m}, epw_* metrics for monitoring and alerting.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: epw.enabled (default false). To enable: set epw.enabled=true in dedicated-values.yaml and tune epw.window_seconds and epw.max_headroom_pct.
Recommended defaults: window_seconds=120, decay_tau_seconds=90, max_headroom_pct=25 for mid-tier tenants.
Watch metrics: epw_active, epw_headroom_pct, epw_reclaimed_count, util_ewma_1m and p99_latency per-tenant.
If you observe sustained epw_headroom_pct > 90% for >10m, consider increasing max_headroom_pct or promote to permanent scale-up.
